Congratulations!! My son is almost 1 now, and I couldn't recommend having one more! You may want to revisit how much baby stuff you actually need, especially if you are paying for it yourself, though. It's up to your comfort level, but I forewent a bassinet and crib and I coslept with a lamby. Others who don't cosleep go the Montessori route and put the baby on a floor mattress from the start, then it's one bed for years. I didn't do any baby containers, either, except a non-powered bouncer and a play pen with changing table, mostly as a travel changing table. I babywear, which helps reduce the need for baby positioners/containers, and I never bought a stroller because of it. Instead of bibs, I just change his clothes after every meal, they're tiny and they fit in any load of wash. I really liked that my high chair separates into a table and chair, though, I definitely recommend that. Especially if you have any interest in Montessori. I also never used pacifiers or bottles, nor a pump, but that may not be possible for some people. I also got a lot of hand me down clothes from friends, which I was not expecting.

Look into elimination communication, it's a huge money and trouble saver on diapers and potty training. Godiaperfree.com has a lot of good resources for free, and even more info for pay if you're inclined. I have done that along with prefold cloth diapers as back up. It was a step that then-Attorney General Eric Holder said the Justice Department was considering for Ferguson, Missouri, after the death of Michael Brown. The city eventually reached an agreement short of that but one that required massive reforms overseen by a court-appointed mediator. The move to defund or abolish the Minneapolis department is far from assured, with the civil rights investigation likely to unfold over the next several months.

On Saturday, activists for defunding the department staged a protest outside Mayor Jacob Frey’s home.
